value.rationale: Showing that the potentially exponential multistage factor is a real worst-case phenomenon, and quantifying its rare-event mechanism and gap from one-shot selection on the same final subspace, is a natural and useful boundary result for an incremental randomized algorithm.
residual_risks: The source preprint is extremely recent and its full text was not retrievable in this run; its public abstract does not advertise product-factor sharpness.

final_claim: For every positive stage partition, the MSARP expected-error product factor \(\prod_i(k_i+1)\) is worst-case sharp as a supremum, including for actual orthogonal CSS error, and singleton staging can approach a \(2^d/(d+1)\) expected-error ratio relative to one-shot ARP on the same final subspace.
limitations: Worst-case supremum through increasingly imbalanced leverage scores; no average-case or high-probability claim. Orthogonal-CSS sharpness uses a small trailing singular-value limit.
